summary: A target-level follow-up of the accepted N.1 packet. Six new declarations identify the Bockstein and descent maps, compute the natural e-invariant kernel and cokernel, determine the diagonal real-place extension rather than its cardinality, and compare the edge-normalised first étale Chern map on torsion. The seven inherited N.5 declarations keep their original ids and ownership. The stage is planned, not closed: exact supplier contracts and remaining source/ownership gaps are recorded; nothing is formalised.

nodes.title: Primary torsion through coefficients and localisation
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, S a finite set of finite places, ℓ a prime, j ≥ 2, O = O_{F,S} and R = O[1/ℓ]. The coefficient Bockstein is a natural isomorphism β_R : K_{2j}(R; Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) → K_{2j−1}(R){ℓ}. Localisation identifies K_{2j−1}(O){ℓ}, K_{2j−1}(R){ℓ} and K_{2j−1}(F){ℓ}; these identifications commute with coefficient maps, enlarging S and pullback along embeddings of number fields (using compatible sets of inverted places). The Bockstein here has degree −1; it is not a tensor-product definition of coefficient K-theory.
hypotheses: S is finite; j ≥ 2; ℓ is prime.
K_{2j}(R) is finite by the inherited finiteness-and-rank theorem.
proofSteps: Use the Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ universal coefficient sequence 0 → K_{2j}(R) ⊗ Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ → K_{2j}(R; Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) → K_{2j−1}(R){ℓ} → 0 from H.6. A finite group tensors to zero with a divisible group, so the Bockstein is an isomorphism. Finiteness is asserted for R, not for K_{2j}(F).

Transport along the inherited N.5/soule-theorem, applied to O and R, to identify the three odd-degree primary subgroups. Alternatively, localisation at the places over ℓ uses L.1/quillen-k-groups: both neighbouring positive-degree residue groups have order prime to ℓ.

Naturality of the coefficient cofiber and the localisation maps gives the commutative squares for S ⊆ S′ and for field embeddings. Use the baseline primary-component subgroup rather than inventing a torsion carrier.
acceptance: For j = 2 this compares K_4(R; Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) with the ℓ-primary subgroup of K_3(R), not with K_4(R) ⊗ Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ.
The statement applies at ℓ = 2 even when F has real places: the real correction enters descent, not this Bockstein.
It does not imply finiteness of any positive even K-group of F.

sources.locator: IV.2.5 and Exercise IV.2.6, printed pp. 280, 283; VI.8.2 proof, printed p. 513 (combined PDF pp. 288, 291, 521)
sources.match: The coefficient exact sequence and its use on a ring of ℓ-integers; use the corrected residue ring recorded in ArithmeticKTheory/E17.

nodes.title: The e-invariant is the descent edge
nodes.statement: With F,S,R,ℓ,j as in primary-bockstein-localisation, choose the same Bott-normalised, G_F-equivariant Suslin identification K_{2j−1}(F^s){ℓ} ≅ Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(j) as in the inherited e-invariant. The degree-zero descent edge ε_R : K_{2j}(R; Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) → H^0_et(R; Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(j)) = W_j(F){ℓ} satisfies ε_R = e_{F,ℓ} ∘ loc ∘ β_R. At odd ℓ, and also at ℓ = 2 when F is totally imaginary, ε_R and hence e_{F,ℓ} are isomorphisms. This identifies the maps, not just the orders of their groups. At ℓ = 2 with real places the equality still holds, while the edge can have kernel or cokernel.
hypotheses: Use one coherent Suslin/Bott coefficient convention on the separable closure and on the descent edge.
The assertion that the edge is an isomorphism is restricted to odd ℓ or totally imaginary F.
proofSteps: Over F^s, Suslin gives K_{2j}(F^s; Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) ≅ Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(j), and its Bockstein identifies it with the primary torsion in K_{2j−1}(F^s); even integral K-groups of F^s are uniquely divisible.

The descent edge is restriction to the geometric point followed by G_F-invariants. The natural Bockstein square with R → F → F^s therefore identifies it with the inherited e-invariant composed with β_R. For ℓ = 2 this factorisation is explicitly stated after Rognes–Weibel Example 1.6.

In the cohomological-dimension-two cases, import from M.7 the Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ descent calculation, including H^2(R; Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(j+1)) = 0 for j ≥ 2. Only H^0 remains in total degree 2j, so the edge is an isomorphism. Natural maps between descent spectral sequences give compatibility with S and field embeddings.
acceptance: For a totally imaginary exceptional field such as Q(√−7), the dyadic edge is still an isomorphism; exceptional cyclotomic image alone does not create a real-place kernel.
For Q and j = 2, e_{Q,2} is surjective with nonzero kernel; replacing the equality of maps by an isomorphism without the cohomological-dimension hypothesis fails.
Changing the Suslin trivialisation changes both sides coherently; no unrelated generator of W_j is declared canonical.

sources.match: Explicit factorisation through the Bockstein and restriction to an algebraic closure, at ℓ = 2.
Suslin equivariance and the cohomological-dimension-two descent argument for each prime.

nodes.title: Normal form of a diagonal elementary two-group extension
nodes.statement: Let w,r be positive integers with 2 | w and r ≥ 1, and E an abelian group in a short exact sequence 0 → (Z/2)^r --ι→ E --p→ Z/w → 0. Suppose that a lift x of 1 ∈ Z/w satisfies w x = ι(1,…,1). Then x has order 2w, E ≅ Z/(2w) ⊕ (Z/2)^{r−1}, and p has no additive section. The lift relation is independent of the choice of x because w annihilates the kernel. The equivalence is an existence statement, depending on a basis of the kernel; it is not an equivalence of the sequence with a split extension.
hypotheses: ι is injective, p is surjective and ker p = im ι.
p(x) = 1 and w x = ι of the nonzero diagonal vector.
proofSteps: Choose a basis of (Z/2)^r whose first vector is the diagonal vector; this is possible because it is nonzero when r > 0.

The generators x and this kernel basis present E with relations 2a_i = 0 and w x = a_0. Exactness shows that these relations give E: every element differs from an integer multiple of x by an element of the kernel, and any relation maps to a multiple of w in Z/w.

Eliminate a_0 to get the direct sum Z/(2w) ⊕ (Z/2)^{r−1}. Since a_0 ≠ 0 and w x = a_0, x has order exactly 2w. Every lift of 1 has the same nonzero w-multiple, whereas a section would give a lift killed by w.
acceptance: w = 8, r = 1 gives a cyclic group of order 16 and no section to its quotient of order 8.
w = 8, r = 2 gives Z/16 ⊕ Z/2; it is not Z/8 ⊕ (Z/2)^2, whose exponent is 8.
Dropping r > 0 or the nonzero diagonal relation allows a split extension; these hypotheses must remain visible.

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.7, final paragraph, printed p. 33
sources.match: The source observes the common abstract isomorphism type; the presented relation identifies the particular diagonal class detected at every real place.

nodes.title: The real-place extension of the e-invariant
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field with real-place set V, r_1 = |V| > 0, and n = 8k+3 ≥ 3, j = 4k+2. Write T = K_n(F)_tors and W = W_j(F), cyclic of even order w = w_j(F). There is a natural short exact sequence 0 → (Z/2)^V --ι→ T --e→ W → 0. Under the identification of each kernel coordinate with the unique nonzero element of Z/2, the pushout along any coordinate V → {v} is the pullback, along W ↪ Q/Z(j) at v, of 0 → Z/2 → K_n(ℝ)_tors → Q/Z(j) → 0; its last map is multiplication by 2 in compatible Suslin trivialisations. Consequently, after choosing W ≅ Z/w and lifting 1 to x, one has w x = ι(1,…,1). The extension class is the diagonal vector in Ext^1_Z(Z/w,(Z/2)^V) ≅ (Z/2)^V. Thus T ≅ Z/(2w) ⊕ (Z/2)^{r_1−1}, with e surjective and no section. The sequence and its real-place coordinates are natural; the cyclic generator and abstract direct sum are not chosen naturally.
hypotheses: F is a number field; n = 8k+3 with k ≥ 0; r_1 > 0.
S-integer versions use the inherited odd-degree localisation isomorphism.
The Ext coordinate description uses a chosen cyclic generator of W; all generator choices give the same mod-two vector.
proofSteps: Use the Bockstein-localisation comparison and M.7’s real descent filtration in degree 8k+4. Its two associated graded groups are H^2(F; Q_2/Z_2(j+1)) ≅ (Z/2)^V and H^0(F; Q_2/Z_2(j)) = W{2}, with kernel identified by restriction to real places. The previous comparison identifies its quotient map with e_{F,2}.

Import Suslin’s real torsion map from M.7: in degree 8k+3 the map K_n(ℝ)_tors → K_n(ℂ)_tors is multiplication by 2 on Q/Z. The map of descent filtrations to every real place identifies the corresponding pushout with its pullback over W{2}. Each coordinate extension is nontrivial, so a lift of a cyclic generator has w_2-multiple equal to the diagonal kernel vector.

For each odd prime, the e-invariant is an isomorphism by e-invariant-descent-edge. Adjoin these cyclic odd-primary factors. Since w/w_2 is odd, the full extension has the same diagonal mod-two class and the same lift relation with w.

Apply diagonal-extension-normal-form to determine the group and nonsplitting. For F ↪ E, restriction takes a kernel coordinate at a real place of F to every real place of E above it; coordinates which become complex vanish. This follows from the natural real-place restriction square. For fixed F, enlargement of S leaves the sequence identified with the field sequence.
acceptance: For F = Q, j = 2 and the inherited w_2(Q) = 24 (weight subscript 2, full order), e has target Z/24, kernel Z/2 and domain Z/48; the certified K_3 example is owned by N.8.
When r_1 = 2 and w = 8, the diagonal class gives Z/16 ⊕ Z/2; the split group of the same order has smaller exponent.
Restriction to a totally imaginary extension kills the real-place kernel, consistently with the dyadic isomorphism there.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.7 and its final proof paragraph, printed p. 33; Theorem 6.9, pp. 33–34
sources.match: Real-place maps identify the extension, not merely its cardinality; the all-coordinate diagonal statement follows by applying the proof to every real embedding.

nodes.title: The kernel and cokernel of the odd e-invariant
nodes.statement: For a number field F, j ≥ 2, n = 2j−1 and finite S, let e : K_n(O_{F,S})_tors → W_j(F) be the inherited map transported to F. If F is totally imaginary then e is an isomorphism. If F has r_1 > 0 real places, its kernel and cokernel are respectively (0,0) for n ≡ 1 mod 8; ((Z/2)^{r_1},0) for n ≡ 3 mod 8; (0,Z/2) for n ≡ 5 mod 8; and (0,0) for n ≡ 7 mod 8. In degree 3 mod 8 the sequence has the diagonal class of real-e-invariant-extension. In degree 5 mod 8, e is injective with image the odd-primary subgroup of W_j(F); here j is odd and |W_j(F){2}| = 2. These are assertions about the actual e-map, natural under enlargement of S and field embeddings, rather than chosen direct-sum isomorphisms.
hypotheses: F number field; S finite; j ≥ 2.
Use the residue class of n, not that of j, to index the four rows.
proofSteps: At every odd prime, and at 2 for a totally imaginary field, use e-invariant-descent-edge; kernel and cokernel vanish primarywise.

For a real field use M.7’s even-degree Q_2/Z_2 coefficient filtration: degrees 8a, 8a+2, 8a+4, 8a+6 give W_{4a}{2}, W_{4a+1}{2} = Z/2, the real-place extension over W_{4a+2}{2}, and zero respectively. Index by n+1 = 2j, excluding degree zero.

Identify the edge with e via the comparison. Degree 8a+4 is real-e-invariant-extension; degree 8a+6 has zero source and target W_{4a+3}{2} = Z/2 by N.4. In the other two rows the edge is an isomorphism.

Reassemble primary components of the finite torsion groups. Combine this map-level table with the inherited finiteness/rank result to recover the inherited two integral structure theorems, without adding duplicate declarations or choosing natural free bases.
acceptance: Real n = 3 has kernel (Z/2)^{r_1}; stating only that e is noninjective loses the required coordinates and extension class.
Real n = 5 has no dyadic torsion although W_3(F){2} is nonzero: its cokernel is Z/2.
The n ≡ 1 row begins at n = 9 in this scope; it makes no assertion about K_1 of S-integers.

sources.locator: VI.9.4–9.5, printed pp. 519–521 (PDF pp. 527–529); VI.2.6, printed p. 474 (PDF p. 482)
sources.match: Even coefficient rows and the integral mod-eight consequences, retaining the maps and correcting the two-primary w convention in ArithmeticKTheory/E20.

nodes.title: The first étale edge Chern map on torsion
nodes.statement: Let F,S,R,ℓ,j be as in primary-bockstein-localisation. Let c_edge : K_{2j−1}(R)^∧_ℓ → H^1_et(R; Z_ℓ(j)) be the first étale Chern map normalised as the ordinary-to-étale K-theory comparison followed by its degree-one edge (the Dwyer–Friedlander normalisation). Let δ : H^0_et(R; Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(j)) → H^1_et(R; Z_ℓ(j)) be the connecting map of 0 → Z_ℓ(j) → Q_ℓ(j) → Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(j) → 0. Then δ identifies W_j(F){ℓ} with the finite torsion subgroup of H^1_et(R; Z_ℓ(j)), and on K_{2j−1}(R){ℓ} one has c_edge = δ ∘ e_{F,ℓ} ∘ loc. In particular c_edge has the same torsion kernel as e, and its cokernel into cohomological torsion agrees with the preceding kernel/cokernel table. This does not identify unnormalised higher Chern classes with e: their factorial/sign conventions require the separate M.8 comparison.
hypotheses: j ≥ 2; R inverts ℓ; S finite.
c_edge is edge-normalised and uses the same coefficient/Bockstein sign as e-invariant-descent-edge.
Completion is the K-spectrum ℓ-adic passage; its odd group agrees with ordinary ℓ-adic completion here by finite generation and the H.6 Milnor/UCT interface.
proofSteps: The cyclotomic character has infinite image on every number field. For positive j its j-th power is nontrivial, so H^0(R; Q_ℓ(j)) = H^0(R; Z_ℓ(j)) = 0. The coefficient long exact sequence embeds W_j(F){ℓ} into H^1(R; Z_ℓ(j)) and identifies it with the kernel of passage to Q_ℓ cohomology. Finite generation of this H^1 is supplied by M.2; that kernel is its torsion subgroup.

Use the natural coefficient triangles on K-theory and étale cohomology and the comparison supplied by M.7. On the even Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ group, its H^0 edge is ε_R. The connecting square therefore gives c_edge ∘ β_R = δ ∘ ε_R. Apply e-invariant-descent-edge and invert β_R.

For completion, the finite coefficient inverse systems are finite (Mittag–Leffler), and the inverse limit of the bounded finite even-group torsion term with multiplication-by-ℓ transitions is zero. H.6 then identifies the odd completed homotopy group with the completion of the finitely generated odd group, preserving its ℓ-primary torsion.

Restrict the formula to torsion and use e-invariant-kernel-cokernel. Naturality of both triangles proves compatibility with S and pullback. The formula contains no assertion about injectivity of a rational or syntomic regulator.
acceptance: At ℓ = 2, for a real field and n ≡ 3 mod 8, the first edge Chern map has kernel (Z/2)^{r_1}; the real defect does not disappear by renaming the comparison.
At ℓ = 2 and n ≡ 5 mod 8, its image on dyadic torsion is zero but H^1(R; Z_2(j))_tors ≅ Z/2.
At odd ℓ the torsion restriction is an isomorphism onto cohomological torsion. An unqualified classical Chern class is not used as a replacement.

sources.match: The first étale Chern class is defined by the comparison followed by the étale spectral-sequence edge; coefficient compatibility is an explicit supplier interface.
The degree-zero coefficient edge factors through torsion; the connecting-square formula is its coefficient-compatible degree-one consequence.

imports.role: Accepted declarations retained verbatim by reference; this follow-up supplements their missing map/extension proof interfaces and does not recreate their nodes.

inheritedRefinements.detail: The inherited finite-coefficient ownership gap now resolves to the existing L.1/k-theory-mod-m, mod-m-products, bott-element, browder-mod-l-ring, quillen-k-groups and finite-field-galois-descent and finite-field-transfer-formulas nodes (all unchecked supplier plans). For the product argument work first at a multiple M of m whose prime-power factors avoid 2,3,4,8. Reduction on positive odd finite-field coefficient groups is onto because integral positive even groups vanish. Pass to F(ζ_M), use Bott powers and coefficient-localisation module compatibility, then the surjective residue transfers and reduction M → m. Do not infer an associative general-ring product at the exceptional moduli merely from m not congruent to 2 mod 4.

New e-invariant-descent-edge supplies the missing agreement with e. edge-normalised-chern-torsion fixes the precise Chern convention, while agreement with the full M.8 higher-class family remains an inherited request; it is not silently discharged. The new nodes do not import the late full M.8 stage.

requests.need: Extend the existing mod-l-homotopy-and-bockstein-sequence node to Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ = colim Z/ℓ^a with inclusion transitions: natural UCT 0 → K_d(R) ⊗ Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ → K_d(R; Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) → K_{d−1}(R){ℓ} → 0 and its degree-minus-one Bockstein. Include compatibility with localisation and with the existing l-adic-completion-milnor-sequence node; no tensor-only definition of coefficient K-theory.

Name the general characteristic-zero separable-closure Suslin interface K_{2j}(F^s; Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) ≅ Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(j), its Bockstein to odd torsion, and Aut(F^s)-equivariance, with coherent Bott normalisation (K-book VI.1.4, VI.1.6–1.7.1). The existing L.2/separable-closure-l-torsion node is only for a nonarchimedean local field at ℓ unequal to residue characteristic, and cannot substitute for arbitrary number-field Galois action.

For j ≥ 2 and R = O_{F,S}[1/ℓ], supply natural Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ descent and H^2(R; Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(j+1)) = 0 at odd ℓ or totally imaginary F at 2, yielding the degree-2j H^0 edge isomorphism. Supply the ordinary-to-étale comparison coefficient triangles and their edge/connecting square, so that the edge-normalised first Chern map has c_edge ∘ β = δ ∘ ε; this early comparison is separate from the full M.8 regulator/Chern family.

Plan the named theorem suslin-real-finite-coefficient-comparison: for n ≥ 1 and m ≥ 2, K_n(ℝ; Z/m) → π_n(BO; Z/m) is an isomorphism (K-book VI.3.1). Include the real-to-complex torsion maps in Table 3.1.1, especially multiplication by 2 in degree 8k+3. This node must precede the named real-place-dyadic-descent-output: the natural Q_2/Z_2 filtration in degree 8k+4 has kernel H^2(F; Q_2/Z_2(4k+3)) ≅ (Z/2)^{real places}, quotient W_{4k+2}(F){2}, and maps to every real place identifying each coordinate extension with the multiplication-by-2 real extension. Supply all four positive even coefficient rows, the α^m real-place restrictions and the approximation input of VI.9.3; table orders alone do not suffice.

Requested scope extension, supplying M.7/suslin-real-finite-coefficient-comparison: real topological K-theory KO and BO, connective real theory, real Bott periodicity and π_n(BO) for n ≥ 1, plus coefficient Bocksteins and the real-to-complex map (degree 8k+4 integral multiplication by 2). The present stage covers complex ku/KU only; it does not yet supply this contract. Propose an early real-topological-k-theory node beside its complex nodes, with H.5:spectra and UPSTREAM:Topological-vector-bundles as foundations. This is not Tau Ceti Clifford-algebra periodicity.

Continuous étale coefficient sequence for Z_ℓ(j), Q_ℓ(j), Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(j), natural connecting maps, finite generation of H^1_et(O_{F,S}[1/ℓ]; Z_ℓ(j)) for j ≥ 2, and identification of its rationalisation with Q_ℓ cohomology. These give H^1 torsion ≅ H^0(Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(j)) once the positive-weight invariant groups over Z_ℓ and Q_ℓ vanish.

Inherited request only: compare the full family of étale higher Chern classes with M.7’s edge-normalised first Chern map, stating the exact factorial/sign factors and coefficient compatibility. The new arithmetic formula is for the edge normalisation, not an unqualified classical higher Chern class. Resolve the inherited late-stage dependency cycle described in restructure before using full M.8 as an implementation prerequisite of the older cd-two node.

Inherited Harris–Segal input: name and prove the finite-field monomial/wreath-product theorem used by K-book VI.1.5–1.5.2 (Harris–Segal 1975, Theorem 3.1), giving surjectivity on ℓ-primary odd K-groups and the cyclic summand of Z[ζ_m] detected at a residue field. Read the original §3; it has not been read for this packet. Finite-field orders and the Bott-element node alone do not prove this summand.

Refine the existing biexact-pairings-and-products and abelian localisation interfaces with finite-coefficient localisation boundary linearity and transfer projection formula, at safe enlarged moduli M, compatible with reduction M → m. The accepted Soulé proof uses these at the Bott-power/transfer step, not merely the existence of integral products.
